substantial.where: moravian-church-after-1815.why, .teaser ('the day slavery ended'), longDescription paragraphs 2 and 3
substantial.problem: The 1834 and 1838 dates are flattened into one. Hamilton's very next sentence says an apprenticeship of four or six years followed 1 August 1834. LA8-1, a sibling row, tells full freedom at midnight on 31 July 1838 ('the negro is free'). Read side by side, the two rows give the end of slavery on two dates without saying why. At the Cape, Hamilton puts the 450 received at Genadendal in the year after emancipation on 1 December 1838. The draft puts them straight after 1834.
substantial.evidence: Hamilton: 'An appren- ticeship of four or six years, according to the class of employ- ment, was however inaugurated'; 'Emancipation went into effect throughout this colony on De- cember I, 1838.' followed by 'As in the West Indies, the church gained large accessions after emanci- pation. At Genadendal alone four hundred and fifty were re- received within one year'.
substantial.fix: why: 'When the British law ending slavery took effect on 1 August 1834, the Moravian chapels of Jamaica filled. The church's own historian, J. Taylor Hamilton, wrote that 'The thankful people thronged the churches'. Full freedom waited four more years, for the law first bound the freed to an apprenticeship. The Moravians had been in the West Indies for a century by then. After 1815 they carried the same mission on in the Cape, in Suriname, in Labrador and, from the early 1890s, north of Lake Nyasa.' (FRE 66). teaser: 'Chapels were full on Emancipation Day.' Paragraph 2: 'In Jamaica the church ran twenty-six schools by March 1834. On 1 August 1834 a law of Parliament ended slavery throughout the British colonies. Hamilton notes that an apprenticeship of four or six years came first. He says the freed crowds spent Emancipation Day 'in a manner worthy of its significance'. By the end of 1835 the church had 8,521 members on the island. That was 1,339 more than a year before.' (FRE 70). Paragraph 3: 'At the Cape the Moravian mission began again in 1792. Hamilton says it had 2,386 members when slavery was ended there on 1 December 1834. The slaves of the colony were fully free on 1 December 1838. In the year after that, Genadendal alone took in four hundred and fifty people. Each case was decided on its own merits.' (FRE 64). Add fact rows for both new quotes.
